source.title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions

accepted.question_text: In branch-cut cosmology, how should the apparent cosmic anisotropy associated with the smoothness problem of small temperature fluctuations be explained consistently, especially in the final stage of contraction where the authors say a negative value of the dimensionless thermodynamic parameter epsilon reverses the scaling behavior of the anisotropy-related ratio while the remaining ratios stay locked in?

evidence.quote: The anisotropy associated with the smoothness problem of small temperature fluctuations has a peculiar solution that still lacks a more consistent explanation.

This is because, in the final phase of the contraction process, choosing the epsilon parameter with a negative value (dark matter?), the scaling behavior of the ratio is reversed, simultaneously assuming the remaining ratios are locked in.

accepted.question_text: If the branch-cut scale factor shrinks only to a finite critical size well above the Planck limit, what is the physical nature of the finite-size transition between the primordial contraction phase and the primordial expansion phase, which the authors describe as a classical leap?

evidence.quote: This finite size limitation of the range, well above the Planck limit, implies in the branch-cut cosmology (de Freitas Pacheco et al., 2023) a leap, of a classical nature, between the primordial phases of contraction and expansion, a topic that needs further investigation in the future.

accepted.question_text: How should branch-cut cosmology be reformulated quantum mechanically, rather than only through leading-order classical equations of motion, so that the intrinsically quantum evolutionary domain near the primordial transition is described more faithfully?

evidence.quote: A quantum approach, more in line with the nature of this evolutionary domain, following a recent proposal Zen Vasconcellos et al. (2021a), is under investigation.

Evidently, most of these questions should not be limited to a classical description of the evolutionary universe, as their nature is intrinsically quantum. These topics are presently under investigation.

accepted.question_text: What is the correct and more internally consistent way to map the evolution of the cut-planes in branch-cut cosmology, so that the time development of the model across its Riemann-sheet structure is described coherently?

evidence.quote: Other aspects to be investigated refer to a more consistent evolution mapping of the cut-planes

accepted.question_text: What are the cosmological consequences in branch-cut cosmology of abandoning a symmetric treatment of the dimensionless thermodynamics connection epsilon(t), and of choosing a different ordering for the values taken by epsilon(t) during the universe's evolution?

evidence.quote: Other aspects to be investigated refer to ... the consequences of adopting a non-symmetric approach regarding the dimensionless thermodynamics connection ε(t), a different ordering of values of ε(t)

accepted.question_text: What role does dark matter play in the evolution of the branch-cut universe, including any role it may have in the contraction-era scaling behavior that the authors connect to the epsilon parameter?

evidence.quote: Other aspects to be investigated refer to ... the role of dark matter in the evolution of the branch-cut universe.

This is because, in the final phase of the contraction process, choosing the epsilon parameter with a negative value (dark matter?), the scaling behavior of the ratio is reversed, simultaneously assuming the remaining ratios are locked in.

accepted.question_text: What concrete predictions does branch-cut cosmology make for the primordial energy-density fluctuation spectrum that seeds later structure formation, and can Cosmic Microwave Background measurements from Planck constrain or test those predictions?

evidence.quote: Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) measurements by the Planck satellite Aghanim & et.al. (2020) offer on the other hand an unprecedented opportunity to constrain and test the branch-cut model, particularly regarding the fluctuations associated to the energy density primordial spectrum, the seeds of all structures in the early universe.

accepted.question_text: If primordial multi-universes were in thermal contact inside a thermal bath and were subjected to a contraction crunch before later decoupling, what thermal evolution would our universe inherit from that earlier multiverse interaction?

evidence.quote: There are also questions regarding the multiverse content. For example, the conjuncture of a thermal contact of primordial multi-universes, immersed in a thermal bath, subjected to a contraction crunch, and the thermal evolution consequences to our universe after decoupling.

accepted.question_text: Within branch-cut cosmology and its multiverse picture, how are the homogeneity of primordial radiation and the average density of matter established strongly enough to support the later formation of the structures observed in the universe today?

evidence.quote: And the ensuing questions, as the homogeneity of the primordial radiation and average density of matter as key elements for the formation of the structures observed today in the universe, among others.
